records.name_note: NC State's dedicated page carries the page title "Buxus sinica (Boxwood, Korean Boxwood)"; its rendered H1 is the bare binomial. Its Common Name(s) list is alphabetized (Boxwood, then Korean Boxwood), the same order as the title parenthetical, and its description prose calls the plant "Korean boxwood". The page lists Buxus microphylla subsp. sinica and Buxus microphylla var. koreana as "Previously known as" names. Its Cultivars / Varieties list holds only var. insularis entries (var. insularis, 'Justin Brouwers', 'Nana', 'Sunburst', 'Wintergreen'), while its Country Or Region Of Origin field gives China, Taiwan. RHS gives the name Korean boxwood to a var. insularis cultivar ("Korean boxwood 'Justin Brouwers'"), so NC State applies the Korean boxwood (var. insularis) name to a species whose range it gives as China and Taiwan. RHS's dedicated Buxus sinica profile renders only the binomial, with no common name, so no admissible source splits on the name.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Problems field lists Problem for Cats, Problem for Dogs and Problem for Horses (its separate Tags row carries #problem for cats #problem for dogs #problem for horses). Its Poison block, under the human-scoped "Poisonous to Humans" heading, gives Poison Severity: Low; Poison Symptoms: "Dogs and cats: vomiting, diarrhea; Horses: colic, diarrhea, respiratory failure, seizures"; Poison Toxic Principle: Alkaloids; Causes Contact Dermatitis: No. A page-top banner outside that block, naming no scope, says "This plant has low severity poison characteristics." NC State names no poisonous plant part and gives no handling warning. Plant Type as rendered: Perennial, Shrub. RHS's dedicated Buxus sinica profile has a Potentially harmful row reading "Harmful if eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling". It names no animal or person, and its advice to wear gloves when handling goes further than NC State's Causes Contact Dermatitis: No, so the two sources differ on handling.
unknowns: NC State's dedicated Buxus sinica page anchors every value field. RHS's dedicated Buxus sinica profile (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/51756/buxus-sinica/details) gives only an H1 binomial with no common name, Synonyms Buxus microphylla var. sinica, Name Status Correct, and a Potentially harmful row ('Harmful if eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling'). It has no size, sun, soil, moisture, pH or hardiness rows, so it supplies no other value. MoBot's Plant Finder refuses this machine and was not read.

is_houseplant is false (set at landing): NC State's Landscape Location field lists Container, Slope/Bank and Walkways, with no Houseplants value, and its USDA Plant Hardiness Zone field reads 4b-9b; the page's note that it 'grows well in containers' is outdoor container culture. No admissible source frames it as a houseplant.

toxic_to_pets true rests on NC State's Problem for Cats / Problem for Dogs tags and its 'Dogs and cats' symptom list; the page names no poisonous plant part and gives no dose. Poison Severity Low is human-scoped.

soil_ph_min/max left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Alkaline (>8.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), and the prose says 'slightly acidic to slightly alkaline pH'; the open-ended bands set no floor or ceiling.

water_regime left null: NC State gives no watering statement. Its moisture signals are the prose 'medium moisture' and 'Its preference is for moist, sandy loam...' (soil adjectives), the structured Soil Drainage values Good Drainage and Moist, and a drought-tolerance trait (Resistance To Challenges: Drought; tag #drought tolerant). None is a watering cadence, and Moist/medium moisture does not support keep_moist. Day-interval and dry-down fields are left null for an in-ground shrub.

soil_drainage moderate comes from NC State's Good Drainage + Moist pair and 'medium moisture and good drainage'; its note that root rot can be a problem in poorly drained soils is consistent with that.

outdoor_sun_exposure uses NC State's structured Light field (Full sun, Partial Shade, mapped to full_sun and part_shade); direct_sun_hours_max left null because no species-specific hour figure is stated beyond the legend text.

Size: NC State's Dimensions block gives Height 2-10 ft and Width 4-20 ft (24-120 in and 48-240 in); the page does not say which cultivar or variety these ranges describe, and the spread range is unusually wide.

chill_damage_f, temperatures, humidity, light foot-candles, fertilizer and pollinators: no admissible-source statement (NC State lists USDA zones 4b-9b, a hardiness rating, not a damage onset; RHS's dedicated profile gives no hardiness rating), so left null.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which common name leads. NC State's dedicated page for Juniperus procumbens leads with Japanese Garden Juniper: its page-title parenthetical reads "Japanese Garden Juniper, Japanese Juniper", and its alphabetized Common Name(s) list shows the same two names in the same order, though its Description prose calls the plant Japanese juniper. RHS's dedicated page for the same taxon renders "decumbent juniper" as the common name beneath its H1 "Juniperus procumbens". This record follows NC State's title and list lead. NC State also lists Juniperus chinensis var. procumbens under "Previously known as"; that is a former name only, and no field here comes from any chinensis record. The 'Nana' and 'Kishiogima' cultivars are listed on the page but supply nothing.
records.toxicity_detail: Handling note only. NC State's page for Juniperus procumbens has no Poison block and no statement naming cats or dogs. Its Tags list carries a '#contact dermatitis' tag, alongside the co-listed tags #deer resistant, #salt tolerant, #lawn alternative, #needled evergreen, #groundcover, #evergreen, #spreading and #slow growing. The Plant Type field reads Ground Cover. The page gives no symptom list, poison parts or severity rating, and says nothing about edibility. toxic_to_pets is left null because no admissible statement names cats or dogs.
unknowns: NC State is the only admissible source with species-level care data for Juniperus procumbens. RHS's dedicated page (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/9601/juniperus-procumbens/details) loads but is a botanical-details profile only: it gives the common name decumbent juniper, the synonym Juniperus chinensis var. procumbens, Name Status Correct and Plant Range W & S Korea, S Japan, with no sun, soil, pH, height, spread, hardiness or toxicity fields. MoBot's host (plantfinder.mobot.org) failed TLS or allowlist access from the sandbox. Clemson HGIC has only a genus-level juniper factsheet, which is not admissible for this species. Every care field therefore rests on NC State alone.
toxic_to_pets is null. NC State has no Poison block here and only a '#contact dermatitis' tag, recorded as a handling note. No admissible statement names cats or dogs.

is_houseplant is false (set at landing): NC State's Landscape Location field lists Rock Wall and Slope/Bank, with no Houseplants value, and its USDA Plant Hardiness Zone field reads 4a-9b. No admissible source addresses indoor culture.

soil_drainage is null. NC State's structured field reads Good Drainage + Occasionally Dry, and the prose says the plant 'prefers a dry, sandy soil' but also 'tolerates a wide range of soils' and does not tolerate wet soils. That is a preference, not a stated sharp or sandy requirement, so fast is not supported. The structured pair does not match the moderate definition (a bare Good Drainage + Moist pair, or tags spanning both dry and wet). A bare well-drained reading is ambiguous.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null. NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Alkaline (>8.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), so there is no closed floor or ceiling, and RHS's dedicated page has no pH field.

water_regime is null. No watering statement exists. The page gives only soil-drainage tags and a drought and dry-soil resistance trait, and a drought-tolerance trait is not a watering regime. water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est and water_estimate_basis are null because this is an in-ground groundcover and no source frames watering that way.

direct_sun_hours_max is null. NC State's structured Light value, 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)', carries the site's generic category definition, which is a minimum rather than a maximum, and the species prose ('Japanese juniper grows best in full sun, in average, well-drained soils.') states no hours.

soil_base garden_bed is set from NC State's in-ground ground-cover framing ('Japanese juniper, because of its size and spread, is typically used as a ground cover that, over time, forms a large, dense mat.'). The page does not use the term garden bed.

Temperatures, humidity, light_fc, fertilizer, edibility, pollinator attraction and chill damage: no admissible source statement was found, so all are null. The USDA hardiness zones 4a-9b are a zone rating, not a damage-onset temperature.
NC State's mature size block is for the species page itself (Height 6-18 in, Width 120-180 in). The 'Nana' cultivar (dwarf, height of 18") is a cultivar figure and was not used.

records.name_note: NC State's dedicated Viburnum plicatum page leads its page-title parenthetical with Doublefile Viburnum, and its alphabetized Common Name(s) list shows the same four names in the same order; that page also absorbs the former f. and var. tomentosum names. RHS's dedicated Viburnum plicatum page is titled with a different common name, Japanese snowball, so the two sources split on the primary name; Doublefile Viburnum is used because it leads the NC State page.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Viburnum plicatum page has no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats or Problem-for-Dogs tag. It carries 'Edible fruit' in its Play Value list, a Problems field of 'Weedy', and the tag line '#aggressive #butterfly garden #deciduous shrub #deciduous #drought tolerant #hedge #butterfly friendly #fall color purple #fall color #shrub #weedy #shrub border #HS304 #bat friendly #moth friendly' (Weedy problem and #aggressive tag carried as stated). RHS's Viburnum plicatum page, under its Potentially harmful heading, says: 'Fruit are ornamental - not to be eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling.' and, on its Pets line, 'Fruit are ornamental; not to be eaten - see the HTA guide to potentially harmful plants for further information and useful contact numbers'. That RHS Pets line names no animal and gives no symptom list, so it does not establish risk to cats or dogs. The two admissible sources disagree on fruit edibility (NC State Edible fruit tag vs RHS not to be eaten).
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder pages (plantfinder.mobot.org) could not be loaded in this session (certificate/connection failure), so no MoBot evidence was used; MoBot's species-level page was not checked.
toxic_to_pets left null: NC State has no Poison block or cat/dog statement; RHS's 'Pets: Fruit are ornamental; not to be eaten' names no animal.

is_edible left null: NC State lists 'Edible fruit' in Play Value, but RHS says the fruit are ornamental and not to be eaten and to wear gloves when handling; the admissible sources disagree, so no bare true/false is given.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), and the Acid band is open-ended; RHS lists pH as Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, so no ceiling is set.

water_regime left null: no watering statement; NC State says plant in moist well-drained soil with mulch and carries a #drought tolerant tag and Drought under Resistance To Challenges, which is a tolerance trait, not a watering instruction. Day-interval and dry-down fields null for an in-ground shrub.

Size: NC State's Dimensions block (Height 8-15 ft, Width 10-18 ft = 96-180 in and 120-216 in) is used; the same page's Description prose says 8 to 10 feet tall and as wide, and RHS gives Max Height and Max Spread 2.5-4 metres (98.4-157.5 in) with a 5-10 year time to maturity. Cultivar sizes (e.g. 'Shasta', 'Trizam') are not used.
direct_sun_hours_max null: only the site-wide light-category legend gives hour ranges; no species-specific prose gives a maximum. NC State partial shade is mapped to part_shade.
soil_base garden_bed reflects an in-ground deciduous shrub; no source gives a potting-mix recommendation.

NC State's Problems field says Weedy and its tag list includes #aggressive and #weedy; carried as stated. NC State also lists Purple Mite under its separate heading 'Viburnum plicatum has some other problems:'.
Temperature, humidity, light footcandle, chill-damage and fertilizer fields have no species-specific admissible support (hardiness zones 5a-8b and RHS H6 are survival ratings, not damage onsets).

NC State's Previously-known-as entries (f. tomentosum, var. tomentosum) are absorbed into this page; NC State and RHS both treat Viburnum plicatum at species level here, so traits of the sterile f. plicatum or of cultivars are not separated.

No field here was borrowed from another taxon's page (the landed Viburnum carlesii, dentatum, nudum and prunifolium records, or forma- and cultivar-level pages); this is a statement about the research process, moved out of name_note at landing, as the audit directed, because no source can support it.

RHS's page title is "Chamaecyparis obtusa | hinoki cypress", and RHS's other common names are "Japanese cypress, tree of the sun".
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden's dedicated page (https://plantfinder.mobot.org/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279589&isprofile=0) fails TLS certificate verification for this machine's command-line fetchers (curl, httpx and WebFetch), so verify_quotes skips it, but it renders in a browser. Its rows read 'Common Name: hinoki cypress', 'Sun: Full sun to part shade', 'Height: 50.00 to 75.00 feet', 'Spread: 15.00 to 25.00 feet', 'Water: Medium' and 'Zone: 4 to 8', and it gives no toxicity, edibility or pollinator information (read by the auditor in a browser; not cited, because the host refuses this machine and the quote checker cannot confirm it). It agrees with common_name, outdoor_sun_exposure and the height range. Its spread minimum (15 ft) is higher than NC State's 10 ft, which the record keeps as the anchor. 'Water: Medium' is a mid-scale row with no watering cadence, so water_regime stays null.

toxic_to_pets, toxicity_detail and is_edible are null: the NC State, RHS and MoBot pages for this species name no cat/dog toxicity and do not address eating the plant (NC State has no Poison block). NC State's only use note is 'Has been widely used in Japanese architecture.'
attracts_pollinators is null: NC State carries a 'wildlife friendly' tag but no Attracts field naming pollinators, and RHS has no pollinator tag on this page.

water_regime is null: neither page has a watering statement. NC State's 'Moist' soil tag and RHS's 'moist but well-drained' soil description are soil adjectives, not watering instructions. water_dry_down_target and the day-interval fields are null for an in-ground tree.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null: NC State gives no pH field and RHS lists pH as 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral', so no bound can be set.

Size: NC State's species Dimensions block ('Height: 50 ft. 0 in. - 75 ft. 0 in.', 'Width: 10 ft. 0 in. - 25 ft. 0 in.') is the anchor and was used. MoBot's dedicated page agrees on height ('Height: 50.00 to 75.00 feet') but reads 'Spread: 15.00 to 25.00 feet', a higher minimum than NC State's 10 ft (read by the auditor in a browser; not cited, because the host refuses this machine and the quote checker cannot confirm it). RHS's Max Height is 'Higher than 12 metres' (open-ended, no usable bound), and its Max Spread of '0.5-1 metres' (19.7-39.4 in) is far narrower than either North American width, so it was not used. Wild-tree maxima were not used either: RHS's description says the species is 'reaching heights of up to 35m', and MoBot gives 120 ft as its height 'in its native habitat'. NC State says 'There are many dwarf cultivars in smaller sizes better suited to home use.' No cultivar sizes were used.

outdoor_sun_exposure is full_sun and part_shade. NC State's structured Light field lists 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)' and 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', and MoBot's structured row reads 'Sun: Full sun to part shade' (read by the auditor in a browser; not cited, because the host refuses this machine and the quote checker cannot confirm it). RHS's Position field lists 'Full sun' only, but it is not a North American structured field, and NC State's North American structured field includes part shade, so part_shade is kept. NC State's prose 'It does best in full sun but can tolerate some shade' is a tolerance aside and added nothing.

is_houseplant is false (set at landing; null is not landable): no admissible source frames it as a houseplant. RHS lists 'Patio and container plants' among its suggested planting locations, an outdoor container use. NC State's Landscape Location field lists Meadow and Recreational Play Area, its zones are 4a-8b, and it says 'This tree is rarely used in landscapes due to its mature size of 50 to 75 feet tall by 10 to 25 feet wide.' and 'Hinoki cypress is best used as a specimen in a meadow or recreational play area.'

soil_base garden_bed is a judgement for an in-ground landscape tree that no source names as a soil mix. The drainage reading uses NC State's 'Good Drainage' + 'Moist' tags and RHS's 'Moist but well-drained', which agree on moderate.

No source states a chill-damage onset temperature, day/night temperature ranges, humidity, light in foot-candles, direct-sun hours or fertilizing guidance. NC State's USDA zones 4a-8b and RHS's H6 are survival ratings, not damage-onset temperatures.

records.toxicity_detail: Source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox, page for Wisteria floribunda. Pets: the page carries the tags #problem for dogs, #problem for horses and #problem for cats, and its Landscape 'Problems' field lists Invasive Species, Problem for Cats, Problem for Dogs, Problem for Horses and Weedy. These Problem-for-Cats/Dogs/Horses tags are separate from the Poison block and come with no symptom list or severity of their own. Poison block (Poisonous to Humans heading, so human-scoped): Poison Severity Low (the page header also says 'This plant has low severity poison characteristics.'); Poison Symptoms 'Vomiting (sometimes with blood), diarrhea, depression if raw seeds are eaten'; Poison Toxic Principle 'Lectin, wisterin glycoside'; Causes Contact Dermatitis No; Poison Part Seeds (the only part listed). Plant Type: Vine. Other tags on the page include #twining, #invasive, #aggressive and #weedy. The page's Insects, Diseases, and Other Plant Problems text says 'The seeds are poisonous.' and the Fruit Description says 'Raw seeds are poisonous but can be eaten once properly cooked.' Edibility row, verbatim: 'The seeds can be eaten ONLY once cooked. Young leaves are commonly cooked and flowers can be eaten raw or cooked (stems removed). However, exercise caution as they are similar to other poisonous wisteria species.' The cooked-only edibility condition does not override the statement that the seeds are poisonous. NC State gives no handling warning. Source: RHS, dedicated page for Wisteria floribunda, Potentially harmful field: 'Harmful if eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling. Pets: Harmful if eaten - for further information and contact numbers regarding pets, see the HTA guide to potentially harmful plants'. The sources disagree. RHS's harm statement names no plant part and makes no edible exception, while NC State lists Seeds as the only Poison Part and its Edibility row calls cooked seeds, young leaves and flowers edible. RHS also gives a handling warning (wear gloves and other protective equipment) that NC State does not, and NC State's Poison block answers Causes Contact Dermatitis No. RHS's Pets line names no animal.
unknowns: NC State is this record's main source. RHS's dedicated page for this exact taxon (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/19123/wisteria-floribunda/details) is cited only for its subtitle and its Potentially harmful field. Its other fields were not landed: Position lists Full sun and Partial shade, and part_shade is left out because NC State's structured Light field gives full sun only and its description says 'It is shade intolerant.'; Moisture reads Moist but well–drained, pH Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, Max Height 4-8 metres and Max Spread 1-1.5 metres. MoBot's dedicated page (https://plantfinder.mobot.org/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=368417) refuses non-browser clients from this machine and is not cited.

is_edible is true but conditional: only the cooked seeds, the cooked young leaves, and the flowers raw or cooked with stems removed are described as edible, while the same page says the raw seeds are poisonous (Poison Part: Seeds) and warns the plant is similar to other poisonous wisteria species. Do not treat the plant as generally edible.

NC State tags contradict each other (#wet soils tolerant vs #wet soils intolerant; Landscape Resistance To Challenges lists Dry Soil and Wet Soil). soil_drainage uses the structured Soil Drainage field, Good Drainage + Moist, which is moderate.
soil_base left null: no source states a soil base, and the page's Soil Texture (Clay, Loam (Silt), Sand) is not a substrate recommendation.
water_regime and the water interval fields left null: NC State gives only soil moisture/drainage tags and tolerance traits, not a watering statement.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State lists only the open-ended band Acid (<6.0), which gives no floor or ceiling.
direct_sun_hours_max left null: the page's structured light value is Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day), which has no maximum. The page also says it is shade intolerant.

Mature height and spread left null: NC State has no Dimensions block for this plant. Its 'Available Space To Plant: 24-60 feet' is a planting-space figure, and the 10 to 25 feet or more of twining along a support is a support dimension, not the plant's own size.

attracts_pollinators left null: the NC State page has no Attracts field, and its wildlife statement ('Wildlife does not utilize this plant because the seed size is very large') is not pollinator evidence.

is_houseplant is false (set at landing; null is not landable): NC State frames it as an outdoor woody vine (Plant Type Vine, USDA zones 4a-9b) and no admissible source frames it as a houseplant. Temperature, humidity, light (foot-candle), chill damage, and fertilizer fields left null: no admissible-source evidence read. The hardiness-zone range on NC State is not a damage-onset temperature.
The Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags have no symptom list or severity attached, and the Poison block's symptoms are scoped to humans by its heading (Poisonous to Humans).

is_edible stays true as researched (the audit did not refute it) but is disputed: RHS's dedicated page says 'Harmful if eaten.' with no plant part named and no edible exception, against NC State's Edibility row; both are reproduced in toxicity_detail.

records.name_note: Landed as Yew Podocarpus, the lead of UF/IFAS ST495's Common name(s) line and the name its prose and figure captions use; the batch was researched as Yew Pine, and no source read leads with Yew Pine. NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized and matches its page-title parenthetical: Buddist Pine (sic), Podocarpus, Shrubby Yew Podocarpus, Southern Yew, Yew Pine, Yew Plum Pine. UF/IFAS ST495 is titled 'Podocarpus macrophyllus: Podocarpus', and its Common name(s) line leads with Yew podocarpus, followed by yew-pine and Japanese yew. RHS's common-name heading is kusamaki (page title 'Podocarpus macrophyllus | kusamaki'), with bigleaf podocarp and Japanese yew as other common names. This is a podocarp (Podocarpaceae), not a true yew (Taxus). Japanese Yew is already this catalog's name for Taxus cuspidata, and the aliases Southern Yew, Yew Pine and Japanese Yew must pull nothing from any Taxus record.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State Plant Toolbox: the Problems field lists Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Dogs and Problem for Horses, and the tags carry #problem for cats #problem for dogs #problem for horses; the cat/dog/horse entries have no severity, symptom list or plant part of their own. A page-top banner beside Phonetic Spelling reads 'This plant has low severity poison characteristics.' and links 'See below' to the separate, human-scoped 'Poisonous to Humans' block, which gives Poison Severity: Low; Poison Symptoms: 'CAUSES ONLY LOW TOXICITY IF EATEN. Nausea, vomiting (colic in horses), diarrhea.'; Poison Toxic Principle: Unidentified; Causes Contact Dermatitis: No; Poison Part: Seeds. Plant Type tags on the same page: Edible, Perennial, Poisonous, Shrub, Tree. The description keeps both conditions: 'While these fleshy red arils are edible, children may be tempted to eat the round seeds, which are poisonous.' Fruit Description: 'Aril's are edible but seeds are poisonous.' Edibility field: 'Fruits may be eaten out of hand or added to pies, cakes, and jellies.' (no preparation times given). Scope disagreement: UF/IFAS ST495 says edible fruits but 'the similarly looking seeds are toxic, therefore it is best to avoid ingesting any part of this tree that resembles fruit', a broader caution than NC State's aril-edible statement. UF/IFAS does not name cats or dogs; the cat/dog evidence is NC State's tags only.

water_regime and watering fields null: no source gives a watering statement; 'moist, well-drained' is a soil description and drought tolerance is only a trait. RHS structured Moisture is 'Moist but well-drained or Well-drained'.

records.name_note: Sources split on the lead common name. NC State's page title parenthetical leads with Asian Star Jasmine, and its Common Name(s) list (Asian Star Jasmine, Asiatic Jasmine, Yellow Star Jasmine) is alphabetized, with the first entry matching the title parenthetical. RHS's page title for the same taxon is 'Trachelospermum asiaticum | Asiatic jasmine'. Landed under NC State's lead. NC State's 'is often confused with' module for this species lists Jasminum and Trachelospermum jasminoides. It is not a true jasmine: NC State and RHS both give its family as Apocynaceae, while NC State's Jasminum page places the jasmines in the olive family (Oleaceae). This record is separate from the Star Jasmine record for T. jasminoides, and no care field was taken from it or from any Jasminum page or record; NC State's Jasminum page is cited only for that family contrast.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: NC State has no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats or Problem-for-Dogs tag for this species, RHS's species profile carries no toxicity statement, and no other admissible dedicated page was found. Nothing was inherited from T. jasminoides or the family.

No dedicated page for this exact taxon was found at plantfinder.mobot.org (a Trachelospermum search there returns only T. jasminoides), at ask.ifas.ufl.edu/edis, or at hgic.clemson.edu (Clemson mentions T. asiaticum only inside multi-species vine and groundcover factsheets). Penn State, UMD and UGA were not searched. Only NC State and RHS carry species pages that were used.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Alkaline (>8.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), which are open-ended at both ends, and RHS lists pH as 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral'.

water_regime and the other watering fields left null: NC State's 'Moist' is a soil-drainage tag, not a watering statement, and the page only lists drought tolerance as a trait. RHS says only 'Well-drained' for moisture. No source gives a watering instruction or interval.
fertilize fields left null: no admissible source states a fertilizing schedule or strength for this species.

is_houseplant is false (set at landing; null is not landable): no source calls it a houseplant. RHS lists 'Conservatory Greenhouse' as a growing location and NC State lists Container and Hanging Baskets (no Houseplants value) as landscape locations, with USDA zones 7a-11b, but neither says houseplant.

attracts_pollinators left null: NC State's Attracts field for this species lists only Songbirds, and its Wildlife Value says 'Attracts songbirds.' Songbirds are not pollinators, and neither source names bees, butterflies or other pollinators for this plant.
is_edible left null: no admissible source addresses eating this plant.

chill_damage_f left null: no source gives a damage-onset temperature. NC State's hardiness zones 7a-11b and RHS's H4 rating are survival or range ratings, not onset figures. Temperature, humidity and indoor light fields are null for the same lack of species-specific source support.

Size conflict, disclosed: mature_height_in and mature_spread_in use NC State's groundcover framing (1-2 ft tall, 10-12 ft wide). RHS lists Max Height 4-8 metres and Max Spread 4-8 metres (157-315 in) for the climbing form. That is a climber-on-support figure, not the plant's own size as a groundcover, so it was not used.

outdoor_sun_exposure: full_sun and part_shade come from NC State's Light field (full sun, and partial shade at 2-6 hours of direct sun) and RHS's Position (full sun, partial shade). NC State's 'heavy shade tolerant' tag and 'Heavy Shade' resistance entry are tolerance statements, so full_shade and part_sun were not added. direct_sun_hours_max is null because the only hour figures are in NC State's site-wide light legend.

soil_drainage is moderate from NC State's bare 'Good Drainage' plus 'Moist' pair. RHS says only 'Well-drained', and NC State's description says 'well-drained average to fertile soils'. soil_base garden_bed is a classification for the in-ground groundcover/vine use. Both sources also allow containers, which would be standard potting: NC State says 'It may be used in the front of the border, in planters, hanging baskets or as a ground cover on sloped areas.' and lists Container and Hanging Baskets among its Landscape Locations, and RHS lists 'Patio and container plants' among its suggested planting locations. No species-specific potting medium is given: RHS's only potting-compost text sits in a conservatory clause of a genus-level Cultivation paragraph that its T. jasminoides page repeats almost word for word.
